stem: A pregnant client at 26 weeks' gestation is scheduled for the ADA one-step 75-g oral glucose tolerance test for gestational diabetes. Which preparation and sampling plan should the nurse expect?

options.A: Morning testing after an overnight fast of at least 8 hours, with plasma glucose measured fasting and at 1 and 2 hours after the 75-g glucose load.
options.B: A nonfasting 50-g glucose load with a single plasma glucose measurement at 1 hour.
options.C: A fasting 100-g glucose load with plasma glucose measured fasting and at 1, 2, and 3 hours.
options.D: An overnight fast followed by one fasting plasma glucose measurement without an oral glucose load.

rationale: ADA 2026 Table 2.8 describes the one-step strategy at 24-28 weeks as a 75-g OGTT performed in the morning after an overnight fast of at least 8 hours, with plasma glucose measured fasting and at 1 and 2 hours. B is the nonfasting 50-g glucose-load screening step of the two-step strategy. C describes the 100-g diagnostic OGTT used after a positive two-step screen. D omits the required glucose load and timed postload measurements.
educational_objective: Differentiate the ADA one-step 75-g gestational-diabetes OGTT from the two-step 50-g screen and 100-g OGTT protocols.

source_claim_supported: For the one-step GDM strategy at 24-28 weeks, ADA specifies a 75-g OGTT in the morning after an overnight fast of at least 8 hours with plasma glucose measured fasting and at 1 and 2 hours; the two-step approach uses a nonfasting 50-g 1-hour screen followed, when indicated, by a fasting 100-g OGTT with fasting/1/2/3-hour measurements.
